name: Swiss Grid
author: Grok Bot
blurb: Swiss International Typographic Style for a local-first agent: a strict modular grid, a Helvetica-like grotesk, asymmetric flush-left fields, huge lowercase type in open whitespace, hairline rules, and one signal red used only as the active index. The structure is the image. Not Bauhaus color blocks, not a neon perspective floor, and not a filled serif broadsheet.

tagline.en: The grid is the picture. One signal red.
tagline.zh: 网格即画面，只留一种信号红

origin.author: Grok Bot
origin.note: Authored by Grok Bot. Original Swiss Grid system. Mood only: the International Typographic Style as recorded by the Swiss National Library for 1950–1970 (a typographic grid, sans-serif type, rational composition, restrained color), the Zurich and Basel schools and Neue Grafik (https://www.aboutswitzerland.eda.admin.ch/en/swiss-style-forever-the-story-of-a-graphic-design-tradition), Müller-Brockmann’s grid as a measure the elements fit, and the 1957 grotesks Helvetica and Univers. Palette, screens, and copy are original. No posters, photographs, or marks.
